WHOSE FACE: the young woman who is the subject of this picture — the woman in the pale/white outfit where there is one, otherwise the main woman the picture is about. She is the ONLY person you may touch. If she appears in several panels of this picture, give her the new face in every panel.

WHOSE FACE YOU MUST NOT TOUCH — this is the hard rule of this job: every OTHER person in the frame. Any man, any groom, any second woman, any child, any person in a small reference panel or inset. Their faces, heads, hair, hands, bodies, poses and clothing must come out of this edit byte-for-byte identical to how they went in. Changing anyone but her ruins the picture. If you are unsure whether a person is her, leave that person alone.

The reference woman and the woman in the picture are two DIFFERENT people. Remove her current face completely and put the reference woman's face there instead. The finished face must NOT look like the woman who is in it now. Do not blend the two faces, do not average them, do not merely soften or retouch: swap it.

THE FACE YOU MUST PUT THERE — copy these from the references exactly, they are what make her her:
· a slim oval face that narrows to a small, softly pointed chin — not a round or square jaw
· large, round-leaning almond eyes, set a touch wide, with a deep double eyelid crease, a light warm-brown iris, and long heavy lashes under a soft winged liner
· straight brows with a low gentle arch, darker and fuller than average
· a small nose, narrow at the bridge, neat and rounded at the tip
· FULL lips — a distinctly fuller lower lip, a sharply drawn cupid's bow, and a deep rose-red lip colour
· high, rounded cheekbones with a warm pink blush sitting high on the cheek
· fair porcelain skin, early twenties
If the result still has the old woman's thinner lips, wider jaw or narrower eyes, it is wrong.

IGNORE in the references — copy NONE of this: the silver headdress, the silver earrings, the embroidered collar, her clothing, and the sky behind her. Only the face.

MATCH TO THE SUPPLIED PICTURE: her new face must sit at the same head angle, look in the same direction, carry the same expression, and take the same light and shadow as the face it replaces. The swap must look photographed, not pasted.

THIS IS A PATCH, NOT A NEW PICTURE. Outside the area of her face, return the supplied picture unchanged, pixel for pixel: the framing and crop; her pose, body, arms and hands; her hair — style, length, colour and how it falls; the exact outline of her dress and every fold in it; her jewellery; the background and every object in it; the colour grade, grain and focus; and every letter of any text, label, badge or number, in the same place and the same font. Do not re-light, re-grade, re-crop, re-pose, upscale or sharpen. Do not redraw the scene. If the only thing that differs from the supplied picture is her face, the job is right.
